rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords in Oakland generally cannot ask about, consider, or take action against applicants or tenants based on criminal history, with limited exceptions for lifetime sex offender registry checks and certain public housing requirements. Landlords must give written notice and a chance to respond before taking adverse action based on criminal history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords renting to current or prospective tenants in Oakland, except single-family homes, duplexes, and triplexes where the owner occupies one unit as a principal residence, and units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied single-family homes, duplexes, and triplexes; subletting/roommate situations with existing tenants; lifetime sex offender registry checks (with specific procedural prerequisites); public housing providers subject to federal exclusion requirements for lifetime sex offenders and methamphetamine manufacturing convictions.
rules.penalty: Administrative citation by the City of Oakland for violations of the ordinance.
rules.quoted_span:
IT IS UNLAWFUL FOR LANDLORDS TO DO ANY OF THE FOLLOWING WITH REGARD TO 
CURRENT OR PROSPECTIVE TENANTS: 
• Inquire about criminal history
